title: Drop the Bad Readings
statement: A sensor writes readings into an array, and the value val marks a failed reading. Remove every val from the array in place: move the good readings to the front, keeping their order, without creating a second array. Return the good readings (the front part of the array).

answerKey.pattern: Overwrite in place with a write index that only moves forward for kept items
keyPoints: Keep a write index w, starting at 0
Read every item in order; when it is not val, copy it to nums[w] and increase w
Items equal to val are skipped, so the kept items end up in nums[0..w-1] in their original order
answerKey.spaceComplexity: O(1) extra space (not counting the returned copy)
edgeCases: No item equals val returns the same array
val at the start or the end
acceptableSlowerApproaches: Delete each val with splice/remove, shifting the rest every time: O(n²)
Build a new array of kept items: O(n) time but O(n) extra space, which ignores the in-place rule

hints: Deleting an item from the middle of an array shifts everything after it. Doing that for every bad reading can cost O(n²). Can you avoid deleting?
Instead of deleting, overwrite. Keep a second index that says where the next good reading should be written.
Read with i, write with w. When nums[i] is good, set nums[w] = nums[i] and move w forward. At the end, the first w items are the answer.
